newsitem.title: USA: Tullett & Tokyo says closes municipal brokerage.
newsitem.headline: Tullett & Tokyo says closes municipal brokerage.

text.p: Tullett & Tokyo Forex Inc said it closed the municipal brokerage department it began slightly more than four years ago, Tim Boyle, president of Tullett & Tokyo in North America said Thursday.

"The closing of the municipal bond operation was a management decision based on the best interests of Tullett & Tokyo Forex," Boyle said. "I would like to add that the entire group displayed a high degree of professonalisim during their years at Tullett & Tokyo, and we wish them all the best in the future."
Eighteen professionals will be laid off, according to market sources.
"These people were some of the best professionals we had in the company, it just came down to a business decision," Boyle said.

Various municipal market participants said the shuttering of Tullett & Tokyo's brokerage department reflected a general lack of secondary market liquidity. The municipal market has too many brokers, and not enough "velocity," one trader said.
"I hate to blame it on the people, they had some good people there," he said. "But they had a number of defections in the last two months too, which doesn't help."
A second market source voiced similar sentiment.

"The people over there were friends of mine, and they were good brokers too," he said. "But there's not enough activity, there's not enough trading, there's not enough spread, there's not a lot of enough things to substantiate a lot of different operations--brokerage, trading, all sorts of things. (It's) a tough business lately."
